learn.hook: Hot sand, very little rain and camels walking slowly: welcome to the Thar Desert!
points: A desert is a dry place that gets very little rain. The Thar Desert is mostly in Rajasthan.
In a hot desert, days are very hot, but nights can be cold.
Many desert houses have thick mud walls and small windows, which keep the inside cool by day. In Kutch, Gujarat, round mud houses are called bhungas.
People save every drop of water. They collect rainwater in underground tanks and step-wells.
The camel is called the ship of the desert. Its wide, padded feet do not sink in sand, and its hump stores fat, not water.

example.q: Think it through: Why do people in the desert wear loose cotton clothes and turbans?
steps: The desert sun is very hot.
Loose cotton clothes let air flow and keep the body cool.
A turban or a covering protects the head from the hot sun and dusty winds.
example.answer: To stay cool and protect themselves from the hot sun and dust.

learn.reallife: If you visit Jaisalmer or Bikaner, look for thick-walled houses, camels and water tanks.

topics.title: Life in the hills and mountains

learn.hook: Snowy peaks, step-like fields and yaks with long hair: let us climb the Himalayas!
points: Hills and mountains are high lands. Places high up are cooler, and some get snow in winter.
Many houses in the hills have sloping roofs, so rain and snow slide off easily. They are often made of wood and stone.
On slopes, farmers cut flat steps into the hillside for farming. This is called terrace farming.
Apples grow in Himachal Pradesh and Jammu and Kashmir. Tea grows on the hills of Darjeeling and the Nilgiris.
People wear warm woollen clothes. In the high Himalayas, yaks give milk, wool and carry loads.

example.q: Think it through: Why do farmers in the hills make step-like fields?
steps: On a steep slope, rain water rushes down.
Rushing water washes away soil and seeds.
Flat steps slow the water and hold the soil.
example.answer: Flat steps stop the soil and water from rushing down the slope, so crops can grow.

learn.reallife: Look at pictures of Shimla, Gangtok or Munnar. Spot the sloping roofs and green step fields!

learn.hook: Waves splash, boats sail out and coconut trees sway: let us visit the seaside!
points: The coast is land next to the sea. India has a long coastline on the west, the east and the south.
Coastal places are often warm and humid (damp air). Many get heavy rain in the monsoon.
Many people living on the coast catch fish, build boats, and grow coconut and rice.
Salt is made from sea water. The sea water is left in shallow pans, the sun dries it, and salt is left behind. Gujarat makes the most salt in India.
Kerala's backwaters are famous for houseboats. Many coastal houses have sloping roofs for the heavy rain.

example.q: Think it through: How does the sun help make salt from sea water?
steps: Sea water is let into shallow, flat pans.
The sun heats the water and it slowly dries up (evaporates).
The salt cannot dry up, so it is left behind as white crystals.
example.answer: The sun dries up the water, and the salt is left behind.

learn.reallife: Next time you add salt to your dal, remember it may have come from the sea and the sun!

learn.hook: Why does a camel have long eyelashes, and why do some houses in Assam stand on stilts?
points: Climate is the usual weather of a place over many years: hot or cold, wet or dry.
To adapt means to change our ways to suit the place we live in. People adapt their houses, clothes, food and work.
In parts of Assam that flood often, some houses are built on bamboo stilts so water can flow under them.
Animals adapt too: camels have long eyelashes to keep out sand, and yaks have thick long hair to stay warm.
Ladakh is a cold desert. It is very cold and dry, with little rain. Pashmina goats there grow very soft, warm wool.

example.q: Think it through: Why would a stilt house be useful in a place that floods?
steps: During floods, water rises over the ground.
A house on the ground would fill with water.
A house on tall stilts stays above the water.
example.answer: The house stays above the flood water, so the family and their things stay dry.

learn.reallife: Compare your clothes in summer and winter. You adapt to the weather too!

revise.summary: Climate is the usual weather of a place over many years. People and animals adapt to it: stilt houses in flood areas, loose cotton in hot places, camels' long eyelashes, yaks' thick hair, pashmina goats in cold Ladakh.
